note: Briefs contain only client-like intent. No expected Story/Visual/Art/Cinema/Editorial/Motion/Sound answers are stored. Production runtime must not import this file.

briefs.brief: A portable induction cooktop brand wants a 30-second film that makes precise heat control feel surprisingly human and useful, without turning into a feature list.
Explain why a B2B SaaS team keeps losing handoffs between sales and implementation, then show the value of one shared launch brief. Do not use dashboard-card storytelling as the default.
A bank needs a short customer explainer for why a card charge can appear pending before it finally posts or disappears. The tone should reduce anxiety without sounding patronizing.
Create a film for a clinic showing why missed appointments create a chain reaction for patients and staff, then end on a constructive scheduling behavior.
Explain how street trees and shade structures change the experience of an extremely hot city block. Make the mechanism understandable without becoming a climate infographic.
A cold-chain logistics company wants to show how one unnoticed temperature excursion can travel through a shipment and become a quality problem later.
A blood-donation nonprofit wants a 30-second film about the gap between intending to donate and actually making an appointment. Avoid guilt-driven messaging.
Explain pay transparency to employees: what it can clarify, what it cannot automatically fix, and why salary ranges still require context.
Show how an AI code-review assistant can catch a risky change while still leaving judgment and responsibility with the engineer.
A warehouse robotics company needs a film explaining why safety zones change when people and autonomous machines share the same aisle.
Explain what a stablecoin reserve attestation can and cannot tell a holder. Avoid coins-flying-through-neon-network clichés.
Explain parametric rainfall insurance to a farmer: payment is triggered by a measured condition rather than a traditional damage inspection.
Explain why a password manager is safer than reusing one memorable password everywhere, without using a generic lock-and-shield slideshow.
A museum wants to explain why conservators sometimes leave visible signs of age on an object instead of making it look brand new.
Explain how a heat-recovery ventilation system can exchange stale indoor air while retaining much of the heat.
A factory wants a short training film showing how a tiny measurement drift can become a large quality problem across repeated production.
An online retailer wants to explain why some returns are refunded instantly while others require inspection first.
Show the emotional and practical difference between a phishing message that creates urgency and a legitimate message that gives the user room to verify.
Explain demand response: why a grid may pay customers to reduce or shift electricity use during a constrained period.
A water utility wants to show how a small hidden leak can be inferred from meter patterns before anyone sees water damage.
Explain spaced repetition to a student without showing a generic calendar or staircase as the central concept.
A regional rail operator wants to explain when a flexible travel pass is better than buying individual tickets, without making the film feel like a pricing table.
A creator platform wants to explain the difference between owning a file, owning copyright, and having permission to use someone else’s work.
Explain why deleting an app does not necessarily delete the account or all server-held data.
A city wants a neutral explainer of congestion pricing: what behavior it is trying to change and why the same road can feel different at different times.
Explain drip irrigation as a distribution problem: getting limited water near roots with less loss than broad surface watering.
A small retailer wants to understand why inventory can be “in stock” in the system but unavailable on the shelf.
Explain compound interest to a young adult in a way that makes time—not money flying upward—the central idea.
Explain why a queue can keep growing even when staff are continuously serving customers, if arrivals temporarily exceed service capacity.
A family-care app wants a short film about siblings coordinating care for an ageing parent: the product should feel like support for the relationship, not the hero replacing it.
